paragraphs.en: Redykołka is a small smoked cheese from sheep's milk, made in Podhale and in the Beskid Śląski. It is usually pressed into the shape of an animal. Shepherds make it from the bundz that is left over when there is not enough for an oscypek.

paragraphs.en: Agnieszka Sancewicz designed the stamp: a cheese animal in front of a carved wooden mould, with a line of sheep above it. The sheetlet margin is drawn in sepia, with flocks, shepherds' huts and a baca, the head shepherd. The series «Polskie produkty regionalne» (Polish regional products) began in 2013. Earlier stamps in it showed the kiełbasa lisiecka and the obwarzanek krakowski.

paragraphs.en: The stamp came out on 15 August, the day of the Polish Armed Forces, which marks the Battle of Warsaw of 1920. Tadeusz Rozwadowski became Chief of the General Staff of the new Polish army on 28 October 1918. From 22 July 1920 he held the post again, through the whole battle.

paragraphs.en: The raspberry 'Polka' was bred at the institute's experimental orchard in Brzezna. It fruits on the canes of the same year. The variety was registered in 2003. The blackcurrant 'Tisel' comes from the institute in Skierniewice itself. It has been in the national register since 2000. The gooseberry 'Biały Triumf' is a traditional dessert variety with pale green fruit.

paragraphs.en: Masovia, the land around Warsaw, was a duchy of its own under a line of the Piast dynasty. Its last dukes were the brothers Stanisław and Janusz III. Stanisław died in 1524. Janusz III died in March 1526. Neither left an heir.

paragraphs.en: On 13 September 1526 the Masovian sejm swore loyalty to King Zygmunt Stary in Warsaw. The Sejm in Piotrków confirmed the incorporation on 24 December 1529. Masovia became a voivodeship of the Crown.

paragraphs.en: The Royal Castle in Warsaw holds a portrait of the two brothers with their sister Anna. It is a copy from about 1620 to 1640 of a painting made around 1520. Above each of them hangs a shield with a white eagle on red.
